definitions.explanation: Reading without vocalizing the words, as opposed to reading aloud. Commonly used in educational settings.

examples.japanese: この{文章|ぶんしょう}を{黙読|もくどく}してください。
{図書館|としょかん}では{黙読|もくどく}がマナーだ。
examples.english: Reading silently is the proper etiquette in the library.

examples.japanese: {音読|おんどく}より{黙読|もくどく}のほうが{速|はや}く{読|よ}める。
examples.english: You can read faster with silent reading than reading aloud.

notes:
CONTRAST:
{黙読|もくどく} (silent reading) is the opposite of {音読|おんどく} (reading aloud). In Japanese schools, both are practiced. {音読|おんどく} is emphasized in language learning because it helps with pronunciation and retention, while {黙読|もくどく} is used for comprehension exercises.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黙読|もくどく}する (to read silently)
- {黙読|もくどく}で{読|よ}む (to read by silent reading)
- {黙読|もくどく}の{時間|じかん} (silent reading time)

KANJI NOTE:
{黙|もく} means silence, as in {沈黙|ちんもく} (silence). {読|どく} means reading.
